subject: night owls
one_liner: Short-form video, exclusively between 11pm and 5am. The feed is closed during business hours.
brand_voice_notes: Sincere founder pitch that treats sleep deprivation as an underserved daypart. Never jokes, never winks. States damning facts in the prose of a shipping notes changelog. The company believes the gate is a feature, the algorithm's honesty is a virtue, and the morning email is a service.

hero.h1: Some content is only good after midnight.
hero.sub: smallhours is a short-form video platform that opens at 11pm and locks at 5am. We don't fight your circadian rhythm. We schedule against it.

features.title: The Gate
features.blurb: smallhours does not open before 11pm local time. Daytime launches show a countdown and nothing else. Demand isn't created here; it's fermented.

features.title: Drowsy Ranking
features.blurb: Every video is scored by its measured ability to keep a tired person awake. High scorers get boosted after 2am, when you're most receptive. This is disclosed here, once.

features.title: The Sunrise Report
features.blurb: Each morning at 7am we email you a complete account of the night. "You viewed 61 videos about canal locks between 3:04 and 4:17." Accountability is a feature. Unsubscribing is not.

testimonials.quote: I learned everything I know about Soviet elevator design between 2 and 4am. My alarm goes off at 6. I would not change a single thing, except most things.
testimonials.name: Priya Raghunathan
testimonials.title: Overnight freight dispatch coordinator, third shift

testimonials.quote: The Sunrise Report ended my marriage, but it was extremely well formatted.

testimonials.title: Former regional print-ad salesman, current night person

testimonials.quote: I tried to open it at noon once. The countdown said four hours, eleven minutes. I sat with that.
testimonials.name: Kelsey Trinh
testimonials.title: Adjunct professor of asynchronous learning

images.rationale: Hero skipped: the design direction is a typographic neon sign, imagery would compete with the glow lockup. Demo is photo-shaped (a video feed of niche night hobbies), so 2 of the budget went to feed stills (canal lock restoration, VHS deck repair). Remaining 2 went to deadpan testimonial headshots (Priya, Doug); Kelsey keeps the CSS initials treatment.

demo_screen_concept: The feed at 3:12 AM: a phone-proportioned vertical swipe feed locked in night mode. CSS-and-photo video cards from hyper-specific niches (canal lock restoration, VHS deck repair, medieval bread) with view counts and a per-video Drowsy Score. A persistent banner ticks down 'time until your alarm: 3h 48m' in real time as you scroll. A 'wind-down mode' toggle dims the screen 4% and does nothing else. The like button is labeled 'this is keeping me awake.' Swiping or arrow keys advance the feed; each swipe silently increments a 'videos tonight' counter the Sunrise Report will cite.

design_direction.style: Retro-futurist neon signage, late-night vacancy dark mode. The page is staged as the marketing site of a heavily funded short-form video company that has decided the hours between 11pm and 5am are an underserved daypart and prices wakefulness by the scroll. A flat near-black violet ground (#0B0714) reads as the sky behind a 24-hour sign: no texture, no grain, only a faint radial haze of neon backwash behind the hero and a thinner one at the footer, so the page reads as a parking lot at 3am rather than a website. Panels are sign cabinets: rounded 16px cards with 1px dim violet borders that brighten and pick up a faint pink outer glow on hover, flat fills a shade lighter than the ground, no blur and no glass. The core motif is the neon tube: the wordmark and one keyword per headline carry a layered pink text-shadow glow, and an OPEN 11PM-5AM vacancy sign sits in the hero, flickering once on load like a tube warming up. One sign pink (#FF3D8A) carries the wordmark glow, every primary CTA, and the live feed-status dot; one rationed all-night cyan (#35E0DC) handles links, the alarm countdown, and secondary highlights, and appears nowhere else. Righteous sets the wordmark and headlines in rounded sign-painter caps with the confidence of a diner that has never closed; Poppins carries plain, faintly investor-deck body copy. Every figure that pretends to be engagement telemetry (videos served, median bedtime slippage, retention past 3am, tier prices) is set in DM Mono with tabular figures inside dim sign wells, so it reads like the meter on the back of the sign, not marketing. Motion is neon-restrained: the vacancy sign flickers once on load (two quick opacity dips), glows pulse on a 6s cycle, cards rise 6px and fade in on scroll with a 40ms stagger, the countdown ticks once per second, CTAs brighten on hover and depress 1px on press, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No light mode, no glass, no blur panels, no clay, no bento lattice, no serifs, no brutalist offset shadows, no terminal chrome, no postal motifs, no emoji. Reads like a company that files sleep under 'churn' and considers your alarm clock a competitor.
design_direction.archetype: Immersive media-feed landing: neon sign hero with the gate stated up front, feature cabinets, telemetry strip, testimonials as motel guestbook entries, pricing as room rates
design_direction.motion_vocab: One-time neon flicker on load; 6s glow pulse; 40ms staggered 6px rise-and-fade on scroll; per-second countdown tick; 1px CTA press depression; all behind prefers-reduced-motion
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Centered sign composition: wordmark as a glowing neon sign, OPEN 11PM-5AM vacancy sub-sign beneath it with the one-time flicker, h1 with a single glowing keyword ('midnight'), radial pink-violet backwash behind, countdown chip in cyan mono under the CTA pair
